About.title: About Hermes
About.intro: How we bring trusted language models together in one chat.
About.overview: Hermes is an interface for chatting with LLMs. We don’t train our own model or present other models as ours. Hermes provides one interface, stores conversation history, and chooses a fallback model when the primary provider is temporarily unavailable.
About.short1: One interface for everyday chat, code, text analysis, photos, and video.
About.short2: Only specific models available in OpenRouter that passed a real API test.
About.short3: The server-side API key is never sent to the browser or shown to the user.
About.short4: Streaming responses, retries, and fallback routing during temporary provider failures.
About.what1: Hermes brings models with different capabilities into one chat. Some are better for photos and video, while others specialize in code, long context, or complex reasoning. The model is fixed to each conversation so its behavior doesn’t change unexpectedly.
About.what2: Hermes also prepares context, sends the necessary attachments, streams the response as it is generated, and stores history so you can return to the conversation.
About.request1: The browser sends text, part of the history, and any required attachments to the Hermes server.
About.request2: The server validates the model and request format, then calls OpenRouter with its own API key.
About.request3: OpenRouter selects available hosting for the chosen model and forwards the request.
About.request4: The response streams back; if a temporary failure occurs before it begins, Hermes can retry or switch models.
About.data1: Guest history is stored in the browser. Signed-in users can sync text history across devices. Files and video frames are sent to a model only when needed for the current request.
About.data2Before: OpenRouter does not log prompt and response text by default, but each downstream provider has its own rules. Do not send passwords, keys, or other secrets in chat. Learn more in the
About.autoText: Auto is local Hermes routing logic, not a separate model or a dynamic OpenRouter catalog. Text and multimodal requests use different short fallback lists. A model without photo or video support is never used for that kind of request.
About.modelsText: The catalog contains only specific versions. We verify OpenRouter availability, zero pricing, supported input formats, and a normal text response through the same API used by the chat.
About.limitsText: As of August 16, 2026, all listed versions have zero-priced input and output tokens in OpenRouter. Free pricing does not mean unlimited capacity: OpenRouter and providers can change daily limits, queues, and availability without notice. Hermes therefore cannot promise unlimited requests.
About.licensesText: Hermes receives responses through an API and does not distribute model weights. The weights remain with providers and are used remotely. Anyone distributing the weights or modified versions must preserve the notices, license copies, and attribution required by Apache 2.0, OpenMDW, and NVIDIA licenses. Direct license links are listed with each model above.
About.limitationsText: Model responses may be inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated. Hermes does not replace professional medical, legal, or financial review. High-stakes answers should be checked against reliable primary sources.
About.freshnessBefore: Availability, limits, and prices of free models can change. The catalog was checked on

Help.title: Help
Help.intro: Everything you need to work confidently with chats, models, files, and your data.
Help.noticeText: Double-check important facts, calculations, and links. A model response is a useful starting point, not a final decision.
Help.startIntro: Your first request only takes three simple steps.
Help.step1Text: Each new chat starts a separate topic. This helps the model keep the right context and makes the conversation easier to find later.
Help.step2Text: Keep Auto if you are unsure, or choose a model for code, analysis, fast answers, photos, or video. The model is fixed to the chat after your first message.
Help.step3Text: Include context, constraints, and your preferred output format. Enter sends the message; Shift + Enter adds a new line.
Help.promptIntro: The clearer your request, the less the model has to guess.
Help.prompt1: State the goal first: describe exactly what the result should be.
Help.prompt2: Include the necessary context, source material, and examples.
Help.prompt3: Set constraints such as language, length, tone, deadline, or format.
Help.prompt4: Ask for missing details to be clarified and refine the result in the same chat.
Help.exampleText: Create a seven-slide presentation outline for beginner designers about typography basics. Give each slide a title and three short points. Use plain English and avoid professional jargon.
Help.featuresIntro: You can combine these tools within a single task.
Help.textFeatureText: Explain topics, edit writing, explore ideas, and work through code. Responses support lists, tables, formulas, and code blocks.
Help.mediaFeatureText: Attach up to four images or videos totaling no more than 3 MB. Hermes prepares key frames from video. A media-capable model is required.
Help.webFeatureText: Turn on Web for requests that depend on fresh information. You should still check dates, sources, and original documents.
Help.imageFeatureText: Describe a scene, choose a format and style, then save the best result in the separate image studio.
Help.dataIntro: Storage works differently depending on whether you are signed in.
Help.guestText: Chats are stored in the browser on this device only. Guests have a limit of five requests per week.
Help.accountText: Text history is available across your devices. Chat titles, favorites, and deletions are synchronized too.
Help.filesText: Photos, videos, and generated images are not synchronized to other devices. They are sent for processing only with the relevant request.
Help.troubleshootingIntro: Quick answers for the most common situations.
Help.attachmentQuestion: Why can’t I attach a file?
Help.attachmentAnswer: Hermes supports PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF images, plus MP4, MPEG, MOV, and WebM video. You can add up to four files totaling no more than 3 MB. If the chat is fixed to a model without media support, start a new chat and select Auto or a multimodal model.
Help.modelQuestion: Why did a different model answer?
Help.modelAnswer: If the selected model is temporarily unavailable before its response starts, Hermes may retry with a compatible fallback. The model that actually answered is shown next to the response.
Help.slowQuestion: Why is the response taking so long?
Help.slowAnswer: Free models can be queued or temporarily overloaded. Wait for the response to begin, stop it if needed, or try again later with another model.
Help.interruptedQuestion: What should I do if a response stops early?
Help.interruptedAnswer: The part already received is preserved. Retry the request or ask the model to continue where it stopped. If the problem persists, start a new chat or choose another model.
Help.storageQuestion: What if my browser runs out of storage?
Help.storageAnswer: Open Settings → Data. You can delete individual attachments, all local files, generated images, or chat history. Removing attachments does not erase the conversation text.
Help.safetyIntro: Do not share anything you would not send to an unfamiliar external service.
Help.safety1: Never send passwords, API keys, banking details, or other secrets.
Help.safety2: Have a qualified professional check medical, legal, and financial decisions.
Help.safety3: For important facts, request sources, open them, and verify the date, author, and content.
Help.stillText: Open a new chat and describe the task, expected result, and what you have already tried.

Hcode.title: Hermes Code
Hcode.intro: The complete guide to hcode v0.1.3 — a fast local terminal AI agent with precise editing, persistent sessions, smart context, automation, and optional GitHub integration. Learn how to install it, connect OpenRouter, navigate a real codebase, control file and command permissions, verify changes, resume long-running work, and use GitHub issues and pull requests without leaving the terminal.
Hcode.noticeTitle: hcode works inside the folder where you start it.
Hcode.noticeText: Open the project directory first, then run hcode. It fixes that directory as the root, keeps file tools inside it, and never starts a background watcher.
Hcode.releaseIntro: This is a major performance, reliability, and project-understanding update. The feature groups below are taken from the published release and verified against the README and source.
Hcode.releaseEditingText: Adds apply_patch, faster code search, reference and related-test discovery, file moves and deletion, and binary-file protection.
Hcode.releaseContextText: A lazy repository map, cached metadata, bounded line reads, and automatic compaction keep the model context focused.
Hcode.releaseSessionsText: Conversations persist by project, --continue and /resume restore them, while /checkpoints and /undo reverse the latest hcode file changes.
Hcode.releasePermissionsText: Safe, Edit, and Auto let you choose a confirmation/speed balance without making dangerous commands or sensitive GitHub actions uncontrolled.
Hcode.releaseAutomationText: Adds one-shot --prompt tasks, JSON output, exit codes, Ctrl+C cancellation, timeouts, retries, and compact handling of large command output.
Hcode.releaseGithubText: hcode can lazily connect to the official github-mcp-server for repositories, issues, and pull requests using only your GITHUB_TOKEN.
Hcode.releasePublishedAfter: ; the v0.1.3 tag and main branch matched when checked.
Hcode.installIntro: The public release contains standalone binaries. Bun, Node.js, and a local build are not required for normal use.
Hcode.installStep1Text: You need macOS or Linux, curl, internet access, a terminal, and an OpenRouter API key. Windows binaries are not currently published.
Hcode.installStep2Text: Paste the command below into your terminal. It detects the operating system and processor architecture, then downloads the matching latest release from GitHub.
Hcode.installStep3Text: Open a new terminal and print the installed version. If the shell cannot find hcode yet, reload its configuration as described below.
Hcode.installerText: It writes the executable to ~/.local/bin/hcode, makes it executable, and adds ~/.local/bin to PATH in ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc when needed. It does not install a package manager or system service.
Hcode.firstRunIntro: Start hcode from the root of the project you want it to work on.
Hcode.firstStep1Text: On the first launch, the prompt hides your input and saves the key to ~/.hcode/config.json. If OPENROUTER_API_KEY is already set, that environment value is used instead.
Hcode.firstStep2Text: Ask in normal language. Include the desired result, relevant constraints, and the verification you expect. hcode responds in the same language as your request.
Hcode.firstStep3Text: Safe is the default: existing-file edits and commands require confirmation. Change it with /permissions after reviewing the rules below.
Hcode.promptExample: Find why the profile form does not save, make the smallest safe fix, and run the relevant tests. Preserve unrelated changes.
Hcode.workflowIntro: hcode combines an OpenRouter model with a local tool registry. It finds focused context first, makes minimal changes, and then runs targeted verification.
Hcode.flow1Text: The directory where hcode was launched is recorded as the project root. File tools cannot move outside it.
Hcode.flow2Text: Your message and conversation context are sent to OpenRouter. By default, hcode uses the openrouter/free route.
Hcode.flow3Text: The model can build a map, search symbols, read line ranges, apply a precise patch, manage files, inspect Git, and run commands. Independent read operations run in parallel.
Hcode.flow4Text: The agent can run up to 20 tool rounds, retry temporary request failures, start with targeted checks, and report completion only after real verification.
Hcode.toolsIntro: The built-in tools cover the full task loop, from understanding an unfamiliar repository through safe edits, diff review, and verification.
Hcode.mapText: Lazily builds a compact import and symbol map for TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, and Rust; unchanged metadata is reused from a local cache.
Hcode.searchText: Searches with ripgrep or a built-in fallback, finds definitions, imports, symbol references, and the tests most likely related to a source file.
Hcode.readText: Reads safe UTF-8 files in bounded line ranges, avoids repeating unchanged reads, and refuses to decode binary files.
Hcode.patchText: Prefers apply_patch to replace one exact unique fragment; it can create or fully write a text file when that is actually necessary.
Hcode.filesText: Creates, moves, and deletes individual files inside the root. Parent traversal, absolute escapes, symlink escapes, directories, and secret files are refused.
Hcode.runText: Runs a command from the project root with a 120-second timeout, stores full output for line-range reads, and returns compact diagnostics to the model.
Hcode.gitText: Shows compact git status and a whole-project or single-file diff so the agent and user can verify only the changes that actually exist.
Hcode.planText: Maintains a short multi-step plan, selects related tests, records command verification, and limits verification retries.
Hcode.modelsIntro: The active model is selected in this strict priority order:
Hcode.modelsChange: /model current prints the active model, /model provider/model-name changes and saves it, and /model without an argument opens an interactive prompt. Changing the model preserves the API key.
Hcode.permissionModesIntro: The mode is saved in config and changed with /permissions safe|edit|auto or the --permission flag for a one-shot task.
Hcode.safeText: Confirms every existing-file edit and every shell command. Read-only operations run without a prompt.
Hcode.editText: Allows safe file changes inside the project but continues to confirm every shell command.
Hcode.autoText: Also auto-allows a small list of safe test, lint, typecheck, build, and read-only Git commands. Other commands are confirmed.
Hcode.permissionsTitle: Safety boundaries remain active in every mode:
Hcode.permissionsText: sudo, system shutdown, mkfs, dangerous device access, and rm -rf are blocked; secret paths are protected. GitHub merges, deletes, push-like actions, and administrative operations always require confirmation.
Hcode.sessionsIntro: hcode stores conversations separately for each project and can continue them after a restart. The project path is hashed and secrets are filtered.
Hcode.session1: Sessions live under ~/.hcode/sessions/; --continue, -c, or /resume loads the latest session for the current project.
Hcode.session2: /compact replaces old verbose tool results with a working summary of goals, files, changes, errors, verification, and plan; compaction also runs automatically near the model limit.
Hcode.session3: The ~/.hcode/cache/ directory stores sizes, mtimes, symbol summaries, and bounded search results—not source contents, environment files, API keys, or credentials.
Hcode.session4: /checkpoints lists up to 20 reversible groups of file actions, while /undo restores only the latest group and refuses to overwrite a file changed after hcode edited it.
Hcode.session5: Prompt history is kept in ~/.hcode/history with a bounded size; hidden input and likely secrets are excluded.
Hcode.automationIntro: -p/--prompt runs one task and exits. --json writes one stdout JSON object with success, message, changedFiles, verification, and usage for scripts and CI.
Hcode.automationSafety: Safe-mode confirmations are never implicitly approved in non-interactive mode. Use --permission edit for permitted file changes; Auto additionally skips only its safe command allowlist.
Hcode.exitCode1: The task is incomplete or verification failed.
Hcode.githubIntro: hcode is an MCP client for the official github/github-mcp-server. The integration does not replace the AI provider: the model still runs through OpenRouter, and hcode works normally without GITHUB_TOKEN.
Hcode.github1: The server starts lazily only for a GitHub request or /github command. hcode first looks in PATH and ~/.hcode/bin.
Hcode.github2: On first use, hcode can download the official native macOS/Linux arm64/x64 binary, verify its published SHA-256, and install it without sudo; Docker is not required.
Hcode.github3: The bounded default toolsets are repos, issues, pull_requests, and users. /github tools lists discovered tools, while /github status verifies the server, protocol, and authentication.
Hcode.github4: /github readonly enables strict server read-only mode; /github readonly off restores read/write discovery. Issue or PR writes need matching token permissions, not admin access.
Hcode.github5: GITHUB_TOKEN is passed only to the MCP child as GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN; it is excluded from command arguments, model context, config, sessions, history, cache, diagnostics, and logs, and redacted from errors.
Hcode.githubPromptExample: Show the open issues for this repository. Read issue #14, fix it locally, and create a pull request after verification.
Hcode.commandsIntro: Slash commands work inside an interactive session. The complete v0.1.3 interface is listed below; launch options are run directly from your shell.
Hcode.commandModel: Print or change the active OpenRouter model; current prints the current value.
Hcode.commandPermissions: Print or switch between Safe, Edit, and Auto.
Hcode.commandContext: Show approximate context use, loaded and modified files, and repo-map state.
Hcode.commandStatus: Show project, model, mode, Git, session, context, plan, and a compact GitHub MCP status.
Hcode.commandUsage: Show request count, input/output tokens, and provider cost when available.
Hcode.commandDiff: Show a summary and diff for the project or an optional file.
Hcode.commandCheckpoints: List reversible groups of hcode file actions.
Hcode.commandUndo: Safely restore the files from the latest hcode checkpoint.
Hcode.commandCompact: Compact the current long conversation into a working summary.
Hcode.commandDoctor: Check Git, ripgrep, Bun, permissions, keys, directories, network, and optional GitHub MCP.
Hcode.commandGithub: Show GitHub MCP; status, tools, and readonly [on|off] are also available.
Hcode.commandResume: Load the latest saved session for the current project.
Hcode.commandClear: Start a new conversation by clearing the screen, conversation, plan, and context state. Project files are not affected.
Hcode.commandVersion: Print the current hcode version inside the session.
Hcode.commandUpdate: Ask for confirmation, install the latest GitHub release, and tell you to restart hcode.
Hcode.commandChange: Replace the OpenRouter API key and use the new key immediately in the current session.
Hcode.commandResetKey: Delete the saved API key. Restart hcode to configure it again.
Hcode.commandVersionFlag: Print the version without starting an interactive chat.
Hcode.commandUpdateFlag: Open the update confirmation without starting a chat.
Hcode.commandContinueFlag: Start hcode with the latest saved session for the current project.
Hcode.commandPromptFlag: Run one task without an interactive chat and then exit.
Hcode.commandJsonFlag: Run a one-shot task and return one structured JSON object.
Hcode.commandPermissionFlag: Choose the permission mode for this launch; especially useful with --prompt.
Hcode.commandDoctorFlag: Run diagnostics without opening an interactive session.
Hcode.configurationIntro: Environment variables override credentials, model selection, GitHub integration, and terminal output without changing saved config.
Hcode.envKey: Uses this OpenRouter key before checking the saved config. Useful for CI or temporary sessions.
Hcode.envModel: Selects a specific OpenRouter model instead of openrouter/free. Use a valid provider/model-name identifier.
Hcode.envGithub: Optionally enables the official GitHub MCP with your Personal Access Token. Never save the token in config.json.
Hcode.envImage: Overrides logo rendering. Accepted values are iterm, kitty, or text; otherwise hcode detects common terminals automatically.
Hcode.envDebug: Set to 1 to print local timing for search, reads, tools, and OpenRouter requests. These timings are not sent as telemetry.
Hcode.envColor: Set this variable to disable ANSI colors in terminal output.
Hcode.securityIntro: hcode is local software, but model requests are processed remotely through OpenRouter. Treat repository access and credentials accordingly.
Hcode.security1: The saved key is stored in ~/.hcode/config.json with user-only file permissions (0600); the ~/.hcode directory is created with mode 0700.
Hcode.security2: The project boundary is validated for file operations, parent path segments are refused, and listed symbolic links are skipped.
Hcode.security3: The file list excludes .env and .env.* secrets, except documented example, sample, and template files. Do not paste secrets into prompts or source files.
Hcode.security4: Review generated code, diffs, and command output. An AI agent can misunderstand a task or produce incorrect code even when a command succeeds.
Hcode.privacyIntro: hcode works locally with files, but messages, selected context, and tool descriptions are sent to the model through OpenRouter. Project code is not uploaded in the background, and there is no watcher or external telemetry.
Hcode.privacy1: ~/.hcode is created with 0700 permissions and config.json with 0600. OPENROUTER_API_KEY takes precedence over the saved key and is not automatically written to disk.
Hcode.privacy2: Automatic discovery, repo maps, and search respect .gitignore and optional .hcodeignore rules. An explicitly named safe ignored file can still be read.
Hcode.privacy3: .env files, private and SSH keys, credentials.json, and service-account*.json remain blocked even when explicitly requested; external paths and symlink escapes are refused.
Hcode.privacy4: Binary reads are blocked, large text is read in small ranges, and command output is reduced for the model while selected lines of the full result remain available.
Hcode.privacy5: Ctrl+C cancels an active operation; OpenRouter requests and shell commands have 120-second timeouts. These are safeguards, not a complete OS sandbox—review diffs and confirmations.
Hcode.updatesText: /update or --update runs the official main-branch install.sh after confirmation and replaces ~/.local/bin/hcode with the latest GitHub release binary. Restart hcode afterward.
Hcode.developmentIntro: Development requires Bun. bun run dev starts src/cli.ts, bun test runs tests, TypeScript handles typechecking, and bun run build creates a standalone dist/hcode for the current platform.
Hcode.releaseCheckedBefore: The current public release is hcode 0.1.3. Repository and release information checked on
Hcode.troubleshootingIntro: Start with hcode doctor. It checks Git, ripgrep, Bun/runtime, config and project permissions, the OpenRouter key, session/cache directories, network access, and GitHub MCP when configured.
Hcode.notFoundText: Restart the terminal or run source ~/.zshrc for Zsh and source ~/.bashrc for Bash. Then check that ~/.local/bin is present in PATH.
Hcode.keyText: Use /change to enter another key for the current session, or /reset-key and restart. Also verify that the key is active in your OpenRouter account.
Hcode.networkText: Run hcode doctor, then check your connection and whether GitHub and openrouter.ai are reachable. Temporary OpenRouter failures are retried up to twice; HTTP status and messages are shown.
Hcode.unsupportedText: The installer currently accepts Darwin or Linux on arm64/aarch64 and x86_64/amd64. Use one of the published platforms or build the project from source with Bun.
Hcode.uninstallText: Remove the installed executable with the command below. This leaves your shell PATH entry and saved API key untouched.
Hcode.configRemovalText: To remove all local data, separately delete the parts you no longer need under ~/.hcode: config.json, sessions/, cache/, history, and optional bin/github-mcp-server. This also removes saved sessions and settings.
Hcode.footerTitle: Read the source, report an issue, or follow releases
Hcode.footerText: hcode {version} is developed openly in tetttet/hcode. The repository contains TypeScript source, tests, the installer, and four published macOS and Linux binaries.
